newsitem.title: JAPAN: Present forex movements excessive-MOF's Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Present forex movements excessive-MOF's Sakakibara.

text.p: Present movements in foreign exchange rates are clearly excessive and do not reflect economic fundamentals, senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official Eisuke Sakakibara said on Wednesday.
"Present exchange rates clearly deviate from economic fundamentals," Sakakibara, head of MOF's International Finance Bureau, told the Lower House of parliament's Finance Committee.
Sakakibara also said movements in the dollar/yen rate over the last few weeks could not be justified by economic fundamentals.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka reiterated that recent exchange rate movements were excessive. "We are concerned and will take decisive measures at an appropriate time," he said.
Sakakibara said market participants' views on the Japanese economy were overly pessimistic and this was reflected in movements in currency markets.

He added that taking into account recent economic indicators, the Japanese economy is highly likely to achieve the government's goal of 1.9 percent growth in the current fiscal year, which began on April 1.
Sakakibara said movements in currency markets were driven by dealers' expectations, which may turn out to be incorrect.
He did not elaborate, but he said expectations that the Japanese economy would remain weak and that Japanese interest rates were going to remain low for some time would lead to a weak yen.
"It is highly likely that these expectations could turn out to be incorrect," Sakakibara said.
He also said that the recent weakening of the yen was not due to higher U.S. interest rates and lower Japanese rates.
